Picked over the Namsangol Hanok Village curated open-air museum because Bukchon's living-village authenticity plus ⟦G0⟧'s craft-shopping commercial appeal cover both 'traditional residential' and 'traditional crafts' narratives in one walk. The private-charter format means the driver-guide can drop at Bukchon's north end (Bukchongil Road) and pick up at the south end near ⟦G0⟧, eliminating backtracking and saving ~10 min vs the bus-tour drop-and-return pattern.

/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en:
Bukchon ('Northern Village') is a 600-year-old hanok (traditional Korean tile-roofed house) residential district nestled between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung Palaces — historically home to high-ranking Joseon Dynasty officials and aristocrats — and today Seoul's largest concentration of preserved hanok homes (~900 traditional houses). 

The signature route walks the **Bukchon 8 Gyeong (8 Famous Views)** with the iconic #6 viewpoint at Gye-dong-gil framing cascading hanok rooftops with N Seoul Tower in the distance — Seoul's most-photographed traditional architecture scene. Bukchon is a LIVING village (not a museum) — residents have publicly requested respectful behavior including quiet hours and limited photography of doorways. 

From Bukchon's southern edge, **⟦G1⟧** (인사동) — Seoul's premier traditional crafts and cultural street — is a 5-10 minute walk. ⟦G1⟧ combines the 4-story spiral **Ssamzigil** complex (70+ craft shops, galleries, cafes, rooftop terrace), traditional teahouses (Mokyeon, Suyeonsanbang), hanji (mulberry paper) workshops, ceramic galleries showing Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain, and Korean souvenir vendors. 

Pedestrian-only on weekends (Sat-Sun). Your driver-guide's flexibility lets you spend more time wherever the group's interest pulls — Bukchon photography vs. ⟦G1⟧ shopping is a natural in-the-moment choice. 

The village's preservation is overseen by **Jongno-gu District Office's ⟦G0⟧ preservation program** — strict zoning rules limit commercial signage, renovation must use traditional materials (handmade hanji paper screens, wooden frames, tile roofs), and the Red Zone entry restriction from 17:00 to 10:00 is enforced by signage and community wardens during peak season.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Bukchon 24/7 (Red Zone restricts tourist entry 17:00-10:00; quiet conduct requested throughout residential lanes); ⟦G0⟧ shops 10:00-22:00

The 4-option menu covers 95%+ of mainstream cruise-passenger preferences without forcing a single choice.

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
Lunch is YOUR choice and timed flexibly around the day's pace — your driver-guide offers three vetted options matched to your group's preferences: **(1) ⟦G0⟧ food alley** — the working-class streetfood experience opened 1905 (Korea's first permanent traditional market), made world-famous by Anthony Bourdain's 'Parts Unknown.' 

Bindaetteok mung-bean pancakes (5,000-7,000 KRW), mayak gimbap, yukhoe raw beef tartare. CASH-ONLY at most stalls. **(2) ⟦G2⟧ traditional restaurant** — sit-down Korean cuisine in a hanok setting; hansik prix-fixe sets featuring banchan (side dishes), bibimbap, kimchi-jjigae stew. 

Mid-tier 15,000-25,000 KRW per person. **(3) ⟦G1⟧ Kyoja or Hadongkwan** — Korean institutions: ⟦G1⟧ Kyoja for handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and mandu since 1966; Hadongkwan for Seolleongtang (oxbone soup) since the 1930s. Mid-tier 12,000-20,000 KRW. 

**(4) Royal court cuisine at Korea House** — premium hanjeongsik (table d'hôte royal cuisine) in a hanok complex (recognized with three ribbons in the 2025 Blue Ribbon Survey); 60,000-120,000 KRW per person, requires 60-min commitment. Communicate dietary needs (vegetarian, halal, no spicy) at booking — driver-guide adjusts accordingly.
